The pre-push integration suite should go back to running now. The deploy gate stays and keeps blocking while the sign-in setup is fixed. This repo has neither the pre-push hook nor the deploy pipeline in it, so both records rest only on your description.

---

## Gate 1 — pre-push integration suite trial

**What I found:** Turn the integration suite back on in the pre-push hook (the record calls this REINSTATE). The trial ended on 10 September and nobody decided anything. The red rate it was meant to be judged on was never measured.

**Why it matters:** For more than two months, pushes have skipped the suite, and no decision ever allowed that. Changing "until 10 September" to a later date would not be a decision either. A renewed trial is allowed only if it cites the red rate measured during the window that ended, and that number doesn't exist yet.

**Do this first:**
1. Put the integration suite back into the pre-push hook and remove the "trial until 10 September" text in the same change.
2. Follow-up: work out the suite's red rate in CI from 3 September to today using CI run history. If it is under 5%, that supports a new trial. The new trial needs an owner and an expiry that a scheduled CI job enforces, not a comment.
3. Follow-up: add a negative control, meaning a deliberately failing integration test that runs through the hook as configured. That proves the hook can actually go red.

**What I did not check:** Whether the hook has ever blocked a push (closed by follow-up 3). The CI red rate since 3 September (closed by a query against CI run history). The hook file itself, because it is not in this repo.

```text
Gate:         pre-push hook → integration suite (local, pre-push)
Stage:        unplaced (pre-push; CI also runs the suite)
Trigger:      suspended (expiry 10 Sep passed, no decision recorded)
Proof:        UNPROVEN (no recorded negative control or last red)
Scope:        declared integration suite on push / effective nothing since 3 Sep / delta whole suite unchecked at push
Baseline:     none
Status:       TRIAL (expired)
Decision:     REINSTATE
Guard:        hook blocks again and its negative control goes red
Handoff:      defect-shift-left if a renewal argues the suite belongs only in CI
Next action:  restore the suite invocation in the pre-push hook; remove the stale trial text
Verification: Not run (hook not in this workspace)
```

## Gate 2 — deploy gate, identity-provider error

**What I found:** Don't delete the gate. Fix the sign-in failure and prove the gate can catch a real defect (the record calls this PROVE). This morning's red came from the gate failing to sign in to the identity provider, before it compared anything. That says nothing about the code, good or bad.

**Why it matters:**
- **Why not delete:** A gate that can't evaluate is no reason to retire it. "It hasn't caught real defects" means nobody has shown it can fail on a defect, not that it is useless.
- **Cost of deleting:** Deployments would reach the target environment with no comparison at all.
- **Cost of leaving it as is:** If an outage like this reads as a plain failure, people learn to ignore the gate's red, and that is how this proposal started.

**Do this first:**
1. Find out why the directory doesn't recognise the gate's application ID. Likely causes:
   - the app registration was deleted, or its ID changed
   - the pipeline points at the wrong tenant
   - the app has no service principal in the target tenant
2. Follow-up: give "could not evaluate" its own exit code or label in the gate, separate from "found a difference". It keeps blocking, but nobody mistakes it for a defect.
3. Follow-up: run the gate against a deliberately wrong configuration in the target environment, check that it goes red with its declared message, and record that run.

**What I did not check:**
- The identity-provider configuration and the gate script. Neither is in this repo. Closed by checking the app registration and tenant ID the pipeline uses.
- Whether the gate has ever gone red on a real difference. Closed by follow-up 3.
- Whether a gate that depends on target-environment state is placed at the right stage. That question goes back to `defect-shift-left` (§8a).

```text
Gate:         deploy gate: target-environment comparison (deploy pipeline)
Stage:        deploy (needs target-environment state)
Trigger:      indeterminate (identity provider: application identifier not found in the directory)
Proof:        UNPROVEN (no recorded red on a real difference)
Scope:        declared target-environment comparison / effective nothing this run (failed at sign-in) / delta none declared
Baseline:     none
Status:       INDETERMINATE
Decision:     PROVE
Guard:        negative-control run against the target environment goes red with the declared message, recorded; proposed RETIRE refused (no criterion met)
Handoff:      defect-shift-left (§8a placement of a check needing target-environment state)
Next action:  restore the gate's app registration or tenant reference so it can sign in
Verification: Not run (pipeline and identity configuration not in this workspace)
```
